key_insight: An optimized gradient boosting model predicted friction stir-welded 7N01 aluminum joint strength with R² = 0.978 and identified process windows targeting at least 90% joint efficiency.
engineering_relevance: The approach provides a quantitative basis for selecting welding parameters to achieve high-strength joints, with shoulder plunge depth helping refine the process window.
method: Predict ultimate tensile strength from rotational speed, welding speed, and shoulder plunge depth.
Compare baseline models, then improve gradient boosting decision trees through grid-search tuning.
Use SHAP to interpret parameter effects and map high-strength process windows.
evidence_signal: Using 27 experimental samples and leave-one-out cross-validation, reported R² increased from 0.905 for the best baseline decision tree to 0.966 for gradient boosting and 0.978 after tuning.
watch_item: The small dataset warrants independent experimental validation before deploying the predicted process windows or extending them beyond the studied conditions.
paper_title: Interpretable ensemble learning for tensile strength prediction and welding process window optimization of friction stir-welded 7N01 aluminum alloy
